clue.text: More hideous fish swallowed her

indicators.note: a fish that has swallowed something holds it inside its body, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted freshwater fish
her is the object form of the pronoun she, used here for the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A grisly fish has gulped a woman down, which makes it even uglier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed' puts SHE inside GAR. 'Gash' is an old Scots word for ghastly or hideous, so its comparative means uglier.
explanation.definitionFit: Gash is an archaic adjective meaning ghastly, so the comparative form is a synonym for uglier.

clue.text: Prepare to obtain prompt

parts.note: to get something is to obtain it
prompt in the sense of quick and willing means ready

explanation.surface: An instruction to make preparations so as to acquire something without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: To make yourself prepared is a common phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Ocean ungulates of the hippocampi type!

parts.note: the ocean is the sea
horses are hoofed mammals, which zoologists call ungulates

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek zoological classification placing marine hoofed beasts in the hippocampus family.
explanation.walkthrough: Hippocampus is the scientific genus name of these little fish, whose heads look like a horse's; the clue pretends they are literally hoofed animals of the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippocampus is the genus of small upright fish with horse-like heads, and hippocampi is its plural.

clue.text: Listens frantically then joins the forces

indicators.note: doing something frantically means in a wild disordered way, so the letters of the preceding word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone hears the call to arms in a panic and signs up for military service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantically' rearranges the letters of 'Listens'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up for military service is to join the armed forces.

clue.text: Silly hint Alan took to make his breathing easier

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, so the letters of the next two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Alan, taking a foolish tip, uses something to help his breathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' rearranges the letters of HINT and ALAN; 'took' is a link pointing to something a person takes.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine breathed in through the nose or mouth is taken to ease congestion and help breathing.

clue.text: Called to see the friend who had put a stop to it early on

definitions.text: put a stop to it early on

parts.note: to call on someone briefly is to nip in, popping into their house
taken as written
bud is American slang for a friend or buddy

explanation.surface: A visitor dropped round to see a pal who had already ended a matter before it got going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nip in' is British informal for making a quick visit. The surface reads as a social call; the definition is the idiom for halting something at its earliest stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from gardening, where pinching a flower bud prevents it developing, so it means stopping something at its start.

clue.text: A cat is beginning to be a believer in very small things

definitions.text: a believer in very small things

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of the word to is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cat is just starting to hold faith in tiny objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' picks the first letter of 'to', giving T; 'be' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of atomism holds that matter is built from indivisible tiny particles.

clue.text: Flabbergast by using a complicated system

parts.note: a maze is an intricate network of paths, so any confusing system

explanation.surface: Someone is dumbfounded by a convoluted arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone completely is a synonym, like astound or stun.

clue.text: Contract to have entertainment at the end of the party

parts.note: a treat is an outing or entertainment provided for someone

indicators.note: the end of the word party is its final letter

explanation.surface: An agreement that guarantees fun when the celebration winds up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the end of' takes the last letter of 'party', Y. 'Contract' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal agreement between nations or parties is a kind of binding contract.

clue.text: Distributor sorts wines when quality of being "interesting" warrants reporting

indicators.note: a distributor spreads goods around, so the letters of the following words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinks wholesaler sorting bottles is so fascinating that the press should cover it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distributor' rearranges the letters of SORTS, WINES and WHEN. 'sorts' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that deserves media coverage has news value, the property of being interesting enough to report.

clue.text: Tow caravan without hesitation along the road

indicators.note: without means lacking, so letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: a trailer is a towed caravan or mobile home
er is the sound of hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: Pulling a caravan smoothly along the highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes ER (a hesitation) out of TRAILER; 'along the road' rounds off the surface picture of pulling something behind a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail something is to drag or pull it behind you, a synonym for towing.

clue.text: Undercover work carried out by sea pigeon, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the preceding words are only one possible arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: Secret intelligence gathered by a seabird carrier pigeon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SEA and PIGEON. Pigeons really were used to carry secret messages in wartime, which lends the surface its plausibility.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying is covert work done to gather secret intelligence.

clue.text: Narcissists, for example, gained nothing but firsts

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
firsts written as 1sts, with the digit one looking like the letter I

explanation.surface: Self-obsessed people, typically, came away with nothing except first places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firsts' is written 1STS, and the numeral 1 is read as I; 'gained' and 'but' join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: People absorbed with themselves are self-centred, which is what an egotist or self-lover is.

clue.text: Well-known artist visits hospital department

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a famous British artist
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A celebrated painter drops in on a section of the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin is a British contemporary artist known for her unmade-bed installation; 'visits' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone distinguished and prominent is famous and widely known.

clue.text: Separation from princess's union

parts.note: Di is Princess Diana, so princess's gives Di's
an association is a union or league of people

explanation.surface: A royal marriage breaks apart, as the princess leaves her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Diana was widely known as Di, and her divorce gives the surface its point.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking a link between things is a separation or detachment.

clue.text: Incitement at the time of compiling

parts.note: on can mean at the time of, as in on arrival
setting is compiling a crossword, done by its setter

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler is accused of stirring up trouble while creating a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword compilers are called setters, so setting a puzzle means compiling it.
explanation.definitionFit: Egging on or urging someone forward is an act of instigation or provocation.

clue.text: First one found…

parts.note: read with the following clue, this is the substance standing first on the periodic table of chemical elements

explanation.surface: Somebody announces the discovery of the very first specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue runs on into 18 Down: the first item 'on the occasional table' is the lightest gas, atomic number one.
explanation.definitionFit: The lightest gas has atomic number one, so it heads the periodic table of chemistry.

clue.text: A testy solution deciphered flamboyantly

indicators.note: deciphering a code means rearranging its scrambled content, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A grumpy answer to a puzzle was worked out in showy fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deciphered' rearranges A, TESTY and SOLUTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a showy, attention-seeking way is the same as acting extravagantly.

clue.text: …on the occasional table

parts.note: an occasional table is a small side table, but read as periodic, it is the chemists' periodic table of substances

explanation.surface: Something is found placed on a small side table.
explanation.walkthrough: This continues 16 Down. An occasional table is a small piece of furniture; 'occasional' stands in for periodic, as in the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: Each entry in the periodic table is a basic chemical substance.

clue.text: Work on a musical drama of note

parts.note: an opera is a drama set to music
te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone is working on a well-known operatic production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work on' looks like the definition phrase, but 'Work' alone defines and 'on a' join it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To function or run, as a machine does, is to work.

clue.text: Firework displayed at champagne pop concert, for instance

parts.note: fizz, also spelt fiz, is informal for champagne
a gig is a live music performance such as a pop concert

explanation.surface: Fireworks were let off at a concert where champagne was flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: A fizgig is an old word for a hissing, spinning firework.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizgig is a small hissing firework, a kind of spinning squib.

clue.text: Middle eastern prime minister was not a Democrat

indicators.note: saying something was not there means removing it, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a 19th-century British prime minister

explanation.surface: A political jibe that a certain premier never belonged to the Democratic party.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian British prime minister; 'was not' removes the D.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the Jewish state is from the Middle East, so the adjective describes that region.

clue.text: Cat found playing in the grass enclosure

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cat was found frolicking in a fenced grassy pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks letters running across 'grass enclosure'; 'found playing' and 'the' are links. A rasse is a small civet of South and Southeast Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The rasse is a small Asian civet, a carnivore loosely called a civet cat.

clue.text: Choose gold cross made by this individual

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A voter decides to mark a gold cross on the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to a voter, who marks a cross on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter marks a cross on a ballot paper, so the cross is made by this person.

clue.text: Alewife enjoys a cigarette with some water

parts.note: gasper is dated British slang for a cheap cigarette
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A woman who runs an alehouse enjoys a smoke along with a drink of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alewife' looks like a pub landlady, but it is a North American herring-like fish. 'enjoys' and 'with some' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Canadian name for the alewife, a herring-like fish of the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Imitating a whistling sound

parts.note: a ping is a short high-pitched ringing or whistling noise, as of a bullet

explanation.surface: Copying a high-pitched whistling noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying others, as monkeys are said to do, is mimicking or imitating.

clue.text: Most weighty trial after king began executing anarchists

indicators.note: after places the trial piece behind the earlier letters

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

indicators.note: where words began means their opening letters are taken

parts.note: a test is a trial

explanation.surface: The heaviest test came when the monarch started putting rebels to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'began' takes the opening letters of 'executing anarchists', EA; GR is George Rex, a royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Most important or most significant is the superlative sense of weightiest.

clue.text: Antibody concerning a spirit

parts.note: re means concerning or about
gin is a distilled spirit

explanation.surface: A medical note about an antibody and a shot of liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Reagin is a type of antibody involved in allergic reactions and the old syphilis test.
